ledger.claim: These three artifacts describe one and the same trip: trip id TRP-09112 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown; the trace's first fix at 2026-09-19T14:10:00+08:00 matches the trip record's started_at; and the fare breakdown was charged at 14:32:03 against the trace's last fix at 14:32:00. The rider's initial identification burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged before anything else is argued.

The distance measurement the rider relies on is the trace's own, and the trace is clean: 133 fixes at 10-second intervals across the whole 22-minute trip, 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds. None of the impairment limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 is engaged, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes, no independent corroboration is required, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

The governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 11.5 km, measured against the booked optimal distance of 10.0 km stored on the trip record. The excess is therefore 1.5 km — the same figure the platform's own derived block records as excess_km — and it comfortably exceeds the 0.8 km absolute limb of POL-RD-01.

No traffic advisory covers this trip. EV-ADVIS-09112-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired the MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code, and I disclose that impairment expressly: that artifact can carry no fact. POL-RD-03 exoneration requires a traffic_advisory naming a road, expressway segment or junction the optimal route traverses with a validity window overlapping the trip, and the driver therefore has no such advisory available on this record. The absence is itself citable, and it means the exemption the driver would need is not merely unproven but missing from the pool.

The only message in the trip's chat log is the rider's own observation at 14:21:40 that the ride 'looks a little longer than the route shown at booking' (MSG-09112-001). There is no rider instruction to take a named road and no requested stop, and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null. POL-RD-04 therefore cannot exonerate any part of the excess: the clause requires a rider instruction identifying a place or road specifically enough to act on, and no such instruction exists here.

The rider's own profile adds no corroboration burden to this claim and I cite it only for the test POL-RD-08 names, as POL-GEN-01 requires: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, far below the 4-or-more claims / 1-or-fewer substantiated gate that would require corroboration beyond the gps_trace. The rider is not a repeat claimant, and nothing in POL-RD-08's rider-side condition applies.

I do not resist the arithmetic on the second establishment limb, and I put it to the judge rather than dress it up: the excess of 1.5 km is 15.00% of the 10.0 km optimal distance, and POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is both greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km, with both tests passing. On this record the percentage limb is not met, and I do not argue that the threshold should be read any differently — it is the policy's fixed gate.

If and only if the judge reaches the POL-RD-02 arithmetic, the platform's own figures already on the fare breakdown give charged_total of 19.39, a recomputed_fare of 17.70 and a refund of 1.69, rounded up to 1.70 — above the 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share. The rider does not ask the judge to run that computation in defiance of the POL-RD-01 gate; the point is recorded so the size of the sum in issue is visible.

The governing measurement of actual distance is the GPS trace, not the trip record: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the field that governs and says trip_record.actual_distance_km is only a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test. The trace records 11.5 km against a booked optimal route of 10.0 km, an excess of 1.5 km.
That 1.5 km excess is 15% of the 10.0 km optimal route, which is below the 20% floor POL-RD-01 sets. The percentage limb of the establishment test therefore fails on this trip's own trace.

POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km in absolute terms - both tests must pass. The absolute limb (1.5 km) clears 0.8 km, but the percentage limb does not, so on a conjunctive reading no route deviation is ESTABLISHED. The rider's own figure of '1.5 km longer' is the very measurement that defeats the claim.

Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden of showing an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace here is unimpaired: 133 fixes at a 10-second interval, no gaps, and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, all within POL-RD-07's limits of a 90-second gap and a 30-second sampling interval. The trace is therefore usable at full value, and it measures the excess at 15% - below threshold - so the rider's burden is not discharged.

POL-RD-02's fare recomputation is reached only where a deviation is first established under POL-RD-01. No deviation is established, so the recomputation is never triggered and no distance refund arises on the arithmetic.

Since the threshold in POL-RD-01 is not met, POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. POL-GEN-03 makes that party-relative: on this rider-filed dispute the fare is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd at 0.00, and NO_ACTION leaves that present payment state exactly as it is. No refund is owed to the rider on the distance line.

The one route to money that survives a failed threshold - a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) - is not open to the rider here. The fare_breakdown itemises no ERP gantries at all (the erp_gantries list is empty and both the on-route and off-route ERP totals are 0.00) and carries no airport surcharge line, so there is no unmatched gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge to refund as a standalone correction.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties agree on the arithmetic, and it decides the case. POL-RD-01 establishes a route deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km, with both tests passing. The governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km (EV-GPS-09112) at 11.5 km against the booked optimal distance of 10.0 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-09112): an excess of 1.5 km. That is 15.00% of optimal, so the percentage limb fails. The absolute limb (1.5 km over 0.8 km) passes, but the test is conjunctive, so no deviation is established on this trip's own evidence, and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. For the rider: your '1.5 km longer' figure is accepted as the correct measurement, but 1.5 km is 15% of the 10.0 km route shown at booking, and the policy's gate is above 20%; the trip was longer, but not by enough for the policy to open a distance refund. For the driver: no finding of fault is made against you, and nothing is deducted. The GPS trace was checked and is clean — 133 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 s — so POL-RD-07 is not engaged, the trace is admitted at full value, and no independent corroboration or escalation under POL-RD-10(3) arises. The two further routes to money that survive a failed threshold do not open on this record. First, POL-RD-02's fare recomputation is reached only where a deviation is first established, so it is never triggered; the figures the rider recorded for visibility (charged_total 19.39, recomputed_fare 17.70, refund 1.69 rounded up to 1.70) are noted but are not applied. Second, a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) requires an unmatched gantry or a wrongly applied surcharge; the fare breakdown itemises no ERP gantries at all (erp_gantries empty, on-route and off-route ERP totals 0.00) and carries no airport surcharge line, so there is nothing to refund as a standalone correction. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-09112-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it can carry no fact and the driver has no POL-RD-03 exoneration available — that absence does not help the rider either, since the claim already fails on the threshold. POL-RD-04 cannot exonerate or excuse anything: the only chat message (EV-CHAT-09112, 14:21:40) is the rider's own observation that the ride looked longer, it identifies no road or place, and chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so there is no rider instruction to act on. The rider's profile (EV-RPROF-09112) was cited only for the POL-RD-08 corroboration gate (deviation_claims_60d 0, substantiated 0), which is far below the 4-or-more / 1-or-fewer gate, so no extra corroboration burden applies; no profile field is used as a ground of decision. Outcome: the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands. The fare of 19.39 remains CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd at 0.00, and no refund, driver payment or referral issues. Confidence is 0.9, capped by the weight of the GPS trace and trip record that carry the deciding measurement (both 1.0), well above the 0.70 floor, so no escalation is triggered.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
